clinician.final_diagnosis: an ulcerated colonic carcinoma at the ileocecal valve
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his mid-70s presented with acute leg weakness, chest pain, and tachycardia, along with chronic left leg pain. Initial physical examination revealed a fever of 39.8°C and a systolic murmur, but the leg weakness had resolved. Initial laboratory tests showed significant anemia (Hb 88 g/L), leukocytosis (15.9 x10^9/L), and elevated CRP (60 mg/L). An echocardiogram, performed due to the murmur and fever, showed continuous spontaneous microcavitations in the right heart chambers but no right-to-left shunt. A CT scan of the chest confirmed these findings and additionally revealed several hypodense hepatic lesions, raising suspicion for metastatic disease. Subsequently, a colonoscopy was performed, which detected an ulcerated colonic carcinoma at the ileocecal valve. The patient refused further examinations or treatment and left the hospital, dying 4 months later.

Echocardiography revealed continuous spontaneous microcavitations in the right atrium, right ventricle, right ventricular outflow tract and truncus pulmonalis, with no right-to-left shunt.
CT scan of the chest confirmed echocardiography findings and showed several hypodense hepatic lesions, suspicious for metastatic disease.
Colonoscopy detected an ulcerated colonic carcinoma at the ileocecal valve.
Patient refused further examinations/treatment and died 4 months after hospital discharge.
